posts.excerpt: Top student cities: London, Manchester, Edinburgh, Birmingham. Intakes in September, January.
posts.content:

posts.title: 10 scholarships international students often miss
posts.excerpt: Many scholarships go unclaimed every year simply because nobody applies. Here are ten types worth checking before you submit your application.
posts.content:
Many scholarships go unclaimed every year simply because nobody applies. Here are ten types worth checking before you submit your application.

Start with the university itself

Most universities offer automatic merit awards of 10–30% for strong grades. Check the international fees page of every university on your shortlist — many awards need no separate application.

Look beyond the big names

Government programmes, professional bodies and charitable trusts all fund international students. Smaller awards of £1,000–£3,000 often have only a handful of applicants.

Mind the deadlines

Some scholarships close a full year before the course starts. Our advisors keep a calendar of deadlines and will remind you in good time.

posts.title: How to write a personal statement that stands out
posts.excerpt: Admissions tutors read thousands of statements every year. These five steps will make yours clear, personal and memorable.
posts.content:
Admissions tutors read thousands of statements every year. These five steps will make yours clear, personal and memorable.

Open with your motivation

Skip the famous quotation. Tell the reader in two or three sentences why this subject matters to you and what sparked your interest.

Show, don’t list

Instead of listing achievements, pick two or three experiences and explain what you learned from them.

Connect to the course

Mention modules or research areas that excite you. It shows you have done your homework.

Ask for feedback

Every Brightway student gets two rounds of feedback on their statement from an advisor before it is submitted.

posts.title: Foundation year or direct entry: which is right for you?
posts.excerpt: Both routes lead to a degree. We compare entry requirements, cost and support so you can choose with confidence.
posts.content:
Both routes lead to a degree. We compare entry requirements, cost and support so you can choose with confidence.

Direct entry

If your school grades and English score meet the university’s requirements, you can start the first year of your degree straight away. It is the fastest and usually the cheapest route.

Foundation year

A one-year programme that combines academic subjects, study skills and English. It suits students whose qualifications are not yet accepted for direct entry, or who want extra support. Over 90% of our pathway students progress to their degree.

Still unsure?

Book a free 20-minute call and we will check your documents against both routes.

posts.title: What to pack for your first year abroad
posts.excerpt: A practical checklist from students who have done it — including the things most people forget.
posts.content:
A practical checklist from students who have done it — including the things most people forget.

Documents first

Passport, visa, offer letter, accommodation contract, insurance and printed copies of everything. Keep them in your hand luggage.

Things worth bringing

A universal adapter, a few favourite spices, medication with a prescription, and one warm coat — you can buy the rest when you arrive.

Things to leave at home

Bedding, kitchen equipment and heavy textbooks are cheaper to buy locally or second-hand from other students.

posts.title: Understanding English test requirements
posts.excerpt: IELTS, PTE, TOEFL or the ELP Test? What universities ask for, what the scores mean and how to prepare.
posts.content:
IELTS, PTE, TOEFL or the ELP Test? What universities ask for, what the scores mean and how to prepare.

What universities ask for

Most undergraduate courses ask for an overall IELTS 6.0–6.5 (or equivalent), with no band below 5.5. Postgraduate and health courses often ask for 6.5–7.0.

Which test should I take?

Check which tests your chosen universities accept before you book. Many now accept several, including online tests taken from home.

Preparing well

Our Language Academy runs four-week intensive preparation courses with a full mock test every Friday.

posts.excerpt: Affordable, friendly and full of opportunities — the study cities our students rated highest this year.
posts.content:
Affordable, friendly and full of opportunities — the study cities our students rated highest this year.

Manchester, United Kingdom

Three major universities, a huge student population and rent well below London.

Dublin, Ireland

A tech hub with English as the main language and a two-year stay-back visa for graduates.

Berlin, Germany

Very low tuition at public universities and a growing number of English-taught master’s programmes.

Melbourne, Australia

Consistently rated one of the world’s most liveable cities, with great part-time work options.

Toronto, Canada

Diverse, safe and home to some of North America’s best-known universities.
